notes:
Account summary: late-stage procurement, but closed-lost to OpenAI direct API. Sales motion ran 09/2024–11/2024; strong product interest but several non-technical decision factors gated us.

Recent timeline:
- 2024-09-12: Lead created (inbound via webinar). Initial discovery call with Amira + Luis. Use-case: personalization + chat support for bookings. Latency target: 150–250ms p95. Throughput: bursty (black-friday-like windows).
- 2024-09-24: Demo (recorded) — showed dedicated pooling and fallback routing. Positive feedback from product manager; CTO asked for security Q&A. Drive: redwood_peninsula_presentation_v2.pdf uploaded.
- 2024-10-07: SE deep-dive (Luis) — proposed VPC + KMS model, can meet data residency and audit logging. Discussed batching/kv caching to hit cost targets.
- 2024-10-22: Security review kickoff — peninsula security team requested SOC2 + penetration checklist. They flagged preference for vendor-managed keys and minimal integration surface.
- 2024-11-05: Final evaluation call (Fireflies ff_20241105_8293). Finance and procurement attended. Peninsula requested TCO comparison vs OpenAI.
- 2024-11-18: Informal check — customer says "execs want the path of least resistance; OpenAI is default."
- 2024-11-28: Last contact — procurement confirms selection of OpenAI direct API. Closed-lost recorded.

Key decision drivers / takeaways:
- Simplicity & brand comfort: execs prioritized the lowest implementation friction. OpenAI perceived as simpler integration (fewer contracts, quicker start).
- No internal champion after headcount shuffle: product sponsor moved to new team; replaced by procurement-focused contact with lower appetite for bespoke infra.
- Security nuance: Peninsula wanted vendor-managed key workflows; our VPC+KMS solution met controls but appeared higher operational lift than their risk appetite allowed.
- Budget timing: freeze on large platform spends for Q4 pushed preference to spot buys vs committed capacity.

POC notes:
- Ran a small POC against embeddings/rerank flow; Redwood latency and quality were fine, costs comparable when batching was enabled. Customer feedback: "tech looks great — but procurement wants the fastest time-to-market."

Next actions (internal):
- Win/loss write-up sent to Product + Security (Dec 2024). Capture friction points around onboarding docs and streamline VPC onboarding.
- Nurture cadence: Q2 2025 re-engage (target new product sponsor, re-evaluate once headcount/budget resets).
- Ask marketing to provide a short one-pager comparing Redwood hosted flow vs direct OpenAI for procurement audiences (focus: contract friction, SLAs, migration path).

Sales snippets / quotes:
- "We liked the reliability and the routing options, but the exec team defaulted to OpenAI for speed of procurement." — PM
- "Security wants to keep keys off-prem and prefers vendor-managed key workflows." — Security lead

Risks/opportunities:
- Risk: account could re-up with OpenAI product commitments (12–24 months).
- Opportunity: if they hit scaling pain points (latency/cost spikes) or need multi-region fallbacks, they may re-contact us. Keep alerts on public comments and partner events.

Support artifacts:
- INF-4029: answered a custom audit question during security review (closed).
- Drive: peninsula_security_qa_2024.xlsx contains the checklist they completed.
status_reason: Lost to OpenAI/Anthropic direct APIs due to exec preference for simpler hosted integration and perceived lower procurement friction.
